neighbours.label: the ending '-ial' in rarer words (glacial, congenial, centennial, jovial, pictorial); weak on everyday -ial words like social, special, material, financial, and silent on look-alike endings like -ual, -eal, -al (ritual, ideal, tidal)
fire: The festival had a jovial, glad mood.
The glacial pace of the negotiations frustrated everyone involved.
Our host was congenial and made every guest feel welcome.
The town held a parade for its centennial celebration.
Grandpa gave a jovial laugh when he opened the gift.
The museum displayed a pictorial history of the railway.
Her tone was rather custodial, as if she were guarding the room.
The judge rejected the argument as merely testimonial in nature.
quiet: The ritual was performed at dawn.
The slow pace of the negotiations frustrated everyone involved.
Our host was friendly and made every guest feel welcome.
The town held a parade for its hundredth anniversary.
Grandpa gave a cheerful laugh when he opened the gift.
The museum displayed an illustrated history of the railway.
The ritual was repeated every evening before dinner.
The judge rejected the argument as merely casual in nature.

notes: Step-out feeder of bonsai1/L1/N6425+ ('racial'), largest single-unit ablation drop (0.20). Test sentences written blind by a second author who saw only the label; the solver's 'leak' (jovial) is actually an -ial word and sits in the fire set.
